subject: Efficiency runbook: pricing, batching/caching guidance & quantization recommendations

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput looked promising. Our procurement lead (Rajiv) asked me to follow up with a few concrete asks as we evaluate pilots:

1) Can you give a short playbook describing how Redwood’s Optimize toolkit would materially reduce token spend for a summary-heavy assistant? Specifically: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization options you recommend for a 2M monthly prompt token baseline.

2) What is typical commercial mechanics for sandbox/pilot credits vs committed discounts? We want a 3-month pilot that can demonstrate latency and cost delta before committing.

3) Do you have any guardrails or known quality regressions when moving from fp16 to 4-bit quant for the family of models you showed?

Attached the questionnaire Rajiv requested. Hoping for a clear short runbook we can circulate internally.

Best,
Sarah

Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up — cost/efficiency asks

Hi Sarah — great to connect. Quick answers up front and a rapid runbook attached. TL;DR: reasonable pilots show 25–45% cost reductions through combined batching + prefix/KV caching; quantization gives another ~20–35% on CPU/GPU ops depending on model and eval drive.

Notes in the draft (attached):
- Batching: aim for adaptive batching with a 50–100ms batching window for chat-heavy flows; use small static priority lanes for requests with <150 token responses to preserve latency. This typically improves throughput without user-perceivable latency.
- KV/prefix caching: cache repeated system prompts and known conversation prefixes; for summary-heavy workloads we often see 30–60% token reuse on second+ messages. Internally we recommend TTL=30m for active sessions and an LRU cap per-user.
- Quantization: start with 8-bit dynamic quant (INT8) for pilot to avoid subtle quality drift, then test 4-bit (QLoRA-style) on a held prompt set. We include evaluation harness suggestions in the runbook.

Commercial mechanics (pilot):
- Sandbox credits: typically 10–25% of expected three-month consumption depending on account profile.
- Commit tiering: step discounts at 3 tiers (baseline, mid, enterprise) with a pilot conversion credit applied at signing.

I’ve attached 1) efficiency_runbook_draft.pdf with recommended configs and 2) a short checklist your SRE can run. If helpful, we can propose a pilot SOW that maps credits to measurable latency/cost SLAs.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Sarah / team — adding a slightly more technical note on quantization and expected quality checkpoints. Priyom’s runbook covers high level but wanted to be explicit: 

1) fp16 -> INT8 path: low risk, usually performance wins on A100 and newer hardware with negligible semantic regression on chit-chat and summarization tasks. Evaluate with 200 prompt holdout and automated ROUGE/BLEU + targeted human checks on 20 edge prompts.

2) INT8 -> 4-bit: aggressive; reduces memory and increases batch density but can introduce hallucination regressions for rare token sequences. We recommend:
   - A/B test with our rollouts tool (5% canary -> 20% -> 100%)
   - Use log-perplexity delta + a small human-reviewed prompt set to gate progression

3) If you have RLHF-style post-training, quantization tends to be less disruptive; if you rely on instruction-tuning only, be conservative.

Attachment: quantified-configs.csv (snippet) — shows expected token/sec uplift and latency deltas by HW type and quant level.

If you want, Monica and I can run an initial inference comparison on a 1k prompt sample you provide. That will give a pragmatic estimate for Lumina’s specific workload.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Applied ML, Redwood Inference

Thanks both — that level of detail is super helpful. Two quick follow-ups from our side: 

A) For the pilot we can commit to a 60-day sandbox where Lumina will send a 10k-prompt sample and a slice of production traffic to measure latency and cost. Is Redwood comfortable with a conversion credit if the pilot shows >=30% cost reduction?

B) Rajiv flagged two procurement items: SOC2 evidence and a simple SOW that maps credits to deliverables (latency targets + monthly cost delta reporting). He also asked if you can provide a conservative estimate for the cost delta if we move straight to 4-bit quant for half our inference volume (we will not immediately move everything — this is to set expectations).

We’ll upload the sample prompts to the shared drive you provided. Can we schedule a 30-minute ops sync early next week to align SRE/infra measures?

—Sarah
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up — cost/efficiency asks

Sarah/Rajiv —

Yes — we can do a 60-day sandbox with a conditional conversion credit: if the measured weighted token cost after recommended batching/caching and the selected quant profile is >=30% lower vs baseline, we apply a one-time credit equal to 25% of the three-month pilot consumption (applied at contract conversion). We’ll bake this into the SOW.

Procurement items:
- SOC2: provide redacted Report and our SOC2 attestation letter (we will include in the docs package).
- SOW: I’ll draft a simple SOW that maps: pilot timelines, credit trigger (>=30% cost delta measured by our shared billing export), latency targets (p99 <= 400ms for median 0–150 token requests), and monthly reporting cadence.

Quant conservative estimate for 4-bit on half volume: based on your 2M monthly baseline, moving 50% of volume to 4-bit (after batching + cache) typically yields incremental 18–28% token-cost reduction on top of batching/cache effects in our benchmarks. Caveats: model family, prompt length distribution, and post-processing can widen that range. We’ll provide a tailored estimate after we run the 1k-sample test.

Next steps:
- I’ll share a first-pass SOW by EOD Wednesday.
- Monica, Connor: please pick two engineers to join the ops sync (30 min) — propose Tue 2028-06-12 09:00 PT or Wed 2028-06-13 11:00 PT.
- Sarah: upload the sample prompts and we’ll start the 1k-run.

Attachments: efficiency_runbook_draft.pdf (with config examples), lumina-procurement-questionnaire.xlsx (filled partial).

Thanks — looking forward to running the numbers with you.

—Priyom
